Overview

mise is a Rust CLI for managing development tools, environment variables, project tasks, and machine bootstrap configuration. A project declares these in mise.toml; mise can install or select tools, expose environment variables, and run tasks in the configured environment.

Public entry points

  • src/main.rs is the primary CLI binary entry point.
  • src/cli contains the public command surface, including exec, run, install, use, activate, task commands, configuration commands, and bootstrap commands.
  • crates/mise-shim/src/main.rs provides a separate shim executable for tool command dispatch.
  • Shell integration is exposed through commands such as mise activate bash, zsh, or fish. Editors and CI can instead invoke the CLI directly.

Core components

  • Command orchestration — src/cli: Maps user-facing commands to tool, environment, task, shell, bootstrap, plugin, and system-management capabilities.
  • Configuration and environment — src/config: Implements project/global configuration, settings, TOML files, version-file discovery, environment directives, trust, and provenance areas.
  • Tool selection and installation state — src/toolset: Represents tool requests, versions, installation options, tool environments, paths, dependencies, and install state.
  • Backend integrations — src/backend: Organizes alternative acquisition and version-resolution backends such as GitHub, HTTP, npm, Cargo, Go, Python, Aqua, UBI, S3, and vfox. The registry directory supplies declarative tool definitions.
  • Task execution — src/task: Loads task files, templates, dependencies, workspace relationships, source freshness, scheduling, output handling, and task caching before running external commands.
  • Shell environment and command dispatch — src/shell: Produces shell-specific activation/deactivation behavior and environment updates. src/shims.rs and the shim crate support command lookup through managed tool installations.
  • Plugin boundary — src/plugins: Hosts core, asdf-style, mise, PackSlip, and vfox plugin integrations. The optional vfox runtime and Lua plugin ecosystem are separately organized under crates/vfox/src and crates/vfox/embedded-plugins.
  • Bootstrap and system management — src/system: Covers machine packages, services, files, repositories, accounts, shell setup, secrets, and system-history operations exposed by bootstrap commands.
  • Reproducibility and persistence — src/lockfile: Handles lockfile generation and graph data; related runtime caching is organized in src/cache.rs.

Relationships

Project or global configuration is interpreted by src/config and supplies tool, environment, and task inputs to the CLI. Tool requests are represented by src/toolset, resolved through a selected src/backend or plugin, and persisted through lockfile/cache facilities. Tasks consume the resulting tools and environment, then execute application-supplied commands. Shell activation and shims expose those resolved tools to interactive shells. The main path is repository code; task scripts, external tools, remote registries, package hosts, shells, editors, and CI are external actors. Plugin implementations may be repository-embedded, installed separately, or supplied by users; the plugin directories define the extension boundary rather than making those implementations part of the CLI core.
